movement_profile.arms_and_hands: Linked in a chain; gestures mimic agricultural tasks like picking leaves.
movement_profile.footwork: Heavy, rhythmic steps designed to create audible sound; includes forward and backward stepping.
movement_profile.formation_and_space: Chain formation moving in expanding and contracting circles.
movement_profile.hips_and_torso: Swinging motion used in the Goddi Beta variation.
movement_profile.levels_and_jumps: Primarily ground-level footwork; no jumps described.
movement_profile.posture: Upright but grounded, with a slight swing in the torso during specific variations.

signature_moves.description: Dancer moves both backward and forward with the swinging of the body.
signature_moves.name: Goddi Beta

signature_moves.description: A ritual movement sequence involving the worship of village deities.
signature_moves.name: Boda Dhimsa

movement_profile.tempo_feel: Steady and driving, synchronized with drum beats.
movement_profile.what_to_avoid: Breaking the chain or losing synchronization with the group's collective footfall.

music_profile.musical_form: Cyclical and repetitive to support continuous group dancing.
music_profile.rhythm_pattern: Heavy rhythmic beats emphasizing the sound of footsteps.
music_profile.sound_description: The sound is dominated by the sharp, percussive strike of the Dappu drum and the high-pitched, melodic wail of the Mori reed instrument, creating a loud and energetic atmosphere.

basic_steps: Form a chain by linking arms or holding hands with 15-20 participants.
Step in synchronization with the Dappu drum beat, emphasizing the sound of the footfall.
Execute the 'Goddi Beta' move by stepping forward and backward while swinging the torso.
Transition the chain from a large outer circle into smaller concentric circles.
Incorporate mimetic gestures such as the 'leaf-picking' hand motion.
teaching.formation: A chain of 15-20 people forming concentric circles.
teaching.level_notes: Beginners start by joining the chain and following the basic circular walk; advanced dancers lead the transitions between the twelve variations.
teaching.rhythm: Driven by the Dappu drum; rhythmic and steady with heavy accents on the footfalls.
